title: Async function prefix
explanation: A JavaScript async function executes its synchronous prefix when called; returning a Promise does not offload CPU work.

title: ES-module microtask context
explanation: This is top-level ES-module execution on the recorded Node version. It is not a universal nextTick ordering rule for CommonJS or every callback context.

title: Promise rejection and side effects
explanation: Promise.all rejects on failure but does not roll back completed effects or automatically cancel other started work.

title: Array of async results
explanation: map preserves callback return values. An async callback returns a Promise; Promise.all collects resolved results in input order.

title: Nested alias after spread
explanation: Object spread copies top-level properties, retaining the nested object reference. This is a memory-alias demonstration, not an authorization grant.

title: Parsed JSON is still untrusted
explanation: JSON parsing establishes syntax, not types, bounds or permission. The supplied role must not become authority; validate the limit before numeric use.

title: Python shared default
explanation: The default list is created once for this function definition. Both calls return the same list; use a fresh per-call value when that is intended.

title: Timestamp meaning
explanation: The explicit source offset permits conversion to UTC. Attaching UTC to an unknown naive timestamp is a different operation and may change its intended meaning.

title: Decimal-string arithmetic
explanation: Binary floating-point cannot represent these decimal fractions exactly. Decimal-string input avoids that initial conversion; precision and rounding policy still matter.

title: Creating a Python coroutine
explanation: Calling Python async def creates a coroutine without running its body. Awaiting it runs the body. Contrast this with the JavaScript async prefix in D01.

title: COUNT rows versus values
explanation: COUNT(*) counts rows; COUNT(column) ignores null values. Do not mix these denominators in reporting.

title: SQLite nullable uniqueness
explanation: This SQLite UNIQUE column accepts multiple NULLs but rejects another nonnull x. Do not transfer this result to a MongoDB index or an explicit NULLS NOT DISTINCT policy.

title: Rollback after a dependent failure
explanation: Both writes are inside one transaction. The duplicate event error rolls back the prior debit. This is local atomicity, not a full payment/external-provider workflow.

title: Async predicate in synchronous filter
explanation: filter tests each returned Promise object for truthiness; it does not await its boolean result. This pattern is especially unsafe for permission filtering.
